authorization: Current owner request (November 2026): the owner reported that in voice Scaramouche talks endlessly and answers silence, ignores "stop" and "Scaramouche leave the voice chat", and that Wanderer never seems to hear them and did not leave when told; they asked to find what was implemented incorrectly, then said "fix them all" to the six proposed repairs.
reason: Live-voice bugs. A sentence ended only after 900 ms of unbroken silence. With noise the speech detector keeps firing on (keys, breathing) a candidate ran to the 12 s cap, so a spoken "stop" was only heard after he had finished, and what Whisper writes for noise ("Thank you.") got an answer. Waiting for "nobody is talking" waited on noise too. Spoken leave accepted only the exact words "<name> leave voice channel". Names were matched exactly and only at the start, so one bot answered lines meant for the other ("Can you hear me, Wanderer?"). The interruption reaction played only if audio was coming out at that instant, not when cut off between sentences. A session whose receiver or speech-to-text had died stayed in the channel, deaf, until someone typed !leave.
replacement: A sentence ends once the last 900 ms are mostly quiet (VOICE_ENDPOINT_SPEECH_RATIO, default 0.35) and counts as speech only with a dense 400 ms stretch (VOICE_MIN_SPEECH_DENSITY, default 0.4); only real speech holds a reply back. Whisper is asked for verbose_json at temperature 0, and segments it rates as silence, repetition loops and its stock silence phrases are dropped. Spoken leave accepts short natural requests ("<name>, leave the voice chat", "leave the call, <name>", and a plain "leave the voice channel" for every bot that hears it), still including the exact phrase, and still refuses negations, questions, "leave me alone" and lines naming the other bot. The shared voice_conversation/names.py matches common misspellings and a closing "..., <name>"; a line addressed to the other bot releases this bot's focus. The interruption reaction also plays when cut off between sentences. When the receiver dies, or when speech-to-text has failed for over a minute (five times or more with no success in between), the bot leaves the channel and posts that it stopped hearing it and that !join brings it back. Interruption modes, DAVE, speaker attribution, greetings, rejoin and text behavior are unchanged. Wanderer's protective character, the opening-only Wander/Wanda address and the voice-only self-edit are unchanged.
privacy_impact: Neutral to positive: less background noise is sent to speech-to-text as speech, and what Whisper makes of it is discarded. Nothing new is collected, kept or shown; the leave notice names no one.
validation: tests/test_voice_live_repairs.py (42 cases, including real-time noise and barge-in runs), updated spoken-leave cases in tests/test_voice_conversation.py, a mutation check that undoes each repair in turn and sees a test fail, a simulated session (silence with noise, stop, stop over noise, spoken leave), old versus new segmenting on the real webrtcvad detector with synthesized speech and generated noise, reviewed voice_conversation file digests with a voice_revision note, preservation and Tarot suites, full offline suite under Python 3.9.25 with SQLite 3.34 rules and on Python 3.11. Not yet tried live in a voice channel.

authorization: Current owner request (November 2026): after a list of ways to make the bots sound more natural in the voice channel, "do 1-6. But for 6, I want it to be a 50/50 chance, or maybe something depending on his mood."
reason: Speech in the voice channel sounded unnatural. Each piece of a reply was sent for synthesis only after the previous one had finished playing, so he paused between pieces; the first piece waited for 100 or more characters; the interruption reaction was synthesized only once he had been cut off; mood was shown by rewriting punctuation, which dropped words ("and" and "but" became full stops) in cold, cutting and angry styles; clips came out at uneven loudness; and every voice reply had "No artificial sentence limit".
replacement: The next piece is synthesized while the current one plays, over a Fish connection kept open per worker thread (one retry on a dropped connection, never on a timeout), and the opening sentence is voiced on its own. The interruption reactions are synthesized ahead of time once the session is idle, and still on the spot when not ready. Each voice style adds a Fish S2 cue before every sentence and a small prosody speed change; the words are left as written, brackets in the reply are removed so only the bot sets cues, a text too long for cues is voiced plainly, and VOICE_EMOTION_TAGS=off restores plain delivery. Live-voice clips are levelled with ffmpeg loudnorm when available (VOICE_LOUDNESS_LUFS, default -18, or off). Each plain conversational reply is short (one to three sentences unless a story or explanation was asked for) with probability 0.5 - 0.03 x his mood toward the speaker (0.8 at -10, 0.5 neutral, 0.2 at +10) and otherwise keeps "No artificial sentence limit"; games, duets and scripted lines keep their length. get_response, get_audio_with_mood and the other locked functions are unchanged.
privacy_impact: None: nothing new is collected, kept or shown. The mood already stored for the person is read to choose the reply length.
validation: tests/test_voice_speech_natural.py (20 cases), a mutation check that undoes each change in turn and sees a test fail, loudness measured on speech clips from -47 to -21 LUFS (all levelled to about -18), the simulated voice session, reviewed voice file digests with a voice_revision note, full offline suite under Python 3.9.25 with SQLite 3.34 rules and on Python 3.11. The cue syntax follows Fish's S2 documentation; not yet heard live.

authorization: Current owner request (November 2026), after reading the live transcript: talking over the bot "should of been always on, but without background noise doing that"; the farewell "should complete his sentence before leaving"; stop words "should also be 'be quiet', 'stop', 'shut up'"; and many transcribed lines were "not what i said".
reason: The transcript showed Whisper inventing Russian and Icelandic words from noise, a full speech in answer to every "Okay." or "Yes.", the memory label "[voice spoken]" copied into replies (even in place of a name), stops missed unless one of a few exact words was heard, and the farewell cut short.
replacement: In KEYWORD mode (the default) real words from the person he is answering, said while he is voicing a reply, stop him as a keyword does; noise (no words), his own echo and listener acknowledgements (okay, yeah, mm-hmm) do not, and NATURAL and OFF modes are unchanged. Stop words add skip, shush, shh, be quiet and a lone quiet. A bare acknowledgement gets no reply unless his last line was a question; games and features still receive it. "[voice spoken]" is removed from what he says. Nothing interrupts the spoken-leave farewell, and he waits 0.5 s after it before disconnecting. Whisper is given the language (VOICE_STT_LANGUAGE, default en; auto restores detection). Unverified DAVE frames are still dropped and are now counted as silence, passed-through voice or other. get_response and the other locked functions are unchanged.
privacy_impact: None: nothing new is collected, kept or shown; the new receive counters are counts only.
validation: tests/test_voice_turns.py, run with discord-ext-voice-recv installed; a mutation check that undoes each change in turn and sees a test fail; reviewed voice file digests with a voice_revision note; full offline suite under Python 3.9.25 with SQLite 3.34 rules and on Python 3.11. Not yet tried live.
